prompt: Tell me my rights under Section 5 Payment of Wages Act.
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant ready to help you with employment, consumer, and tenancy matters.

### | Your Situation
You are seeking clarity on your statutory entitlements and employer obligations regarding the timely disbursement of wages under Indian labor legislation. Understanding these rules helps ensure you are paid fairly and promptly for your labor.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages for every person employed upon or in any railway, factory, or industrial or other establishment must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period in respect of which the wages are payable (if the establishment employs less than 1,000 workers).
* If an establishment employs 1,000 or more persons, Section 5 mandates that wages must be paid before the expiry of the 10th day after the wage period.
* Furthermore, under Section 7 of the Act, deductions from your wages can only be made in accordance with authorized statutory heads (such as taxes or provident fund), and arbitrary or unauthorized salary cuts are strictly prohibited.
* If your employer delays wage payments or makes unauthorized deductions, Section 15 of the Act allows you to file an application before the designated Labour Authority for recovery of wages along with compensation up to ten times the delayed amount.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your employment contract, salary slips, bank statements, appointment letter, and any written communication regarding your unpaid wages.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer demanding the unpaid wages and granting a clear 15-day window to clear the dues.
3. If the employer fails to pay within 15 days, approach the designated Labour Commissioner or Authority under Section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, or file an application under Section 33C(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 before the Labour Court.

### Information I still need from you
1. How many total employees work at your establishment, and exactly how many days of salary are currently delayed?
2. Did your employer provide any written reason or notice for the delayed wage payment or salary deduction?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Recovery of money due from an employer
citations.description: Where any workman is entitled to receive from the employer any money or any benefit which is capable of being computed in terms of money, the workman may apply to the Labour Court for recovery.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.
